messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: High error-rate spike — kv_prefix_cache throughput anomaly in us-west1. 5xx rate up ~3.2x, continuous-batching queue depth spiking, eviction storm observed. Pager routed to cara and sre-oncall.

cara: on it. looking at dashboards now. tagging eng-runtime and devon. 

cara: quick note — is anyone aware of recent tokenizer/hash changes in the last 24h? this looks like a prefix miss amplification.

leo: seeing lots of cache misses with identical prefixes but different prompt hashes. request_rate for prefix-cache up 8x. curious if hashing salt / template normalization changed. logs: `prefix_lookup_miss_count` jumped at 14:03 PDT.

devon: i rolled a small normalization tweak earlier (rolled at 09:30 PDT) that strips repeated whitespace differently. commit: `a1f3c9e`. it touched `prompt_normalizer` and `prefix_key_v2`. didn't think it would change hash.

eng-runtime: ok probable cause: tokenizer normalization + hash encoding drift => formerly-coalesced prefixes now generate distinct keys, massively increasing cache cardinality and blowing memory -> eviction -> more misses -> more compute. pattern matches.

cara: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable continuous batching in affected pool (us-west1) 2) throttle incoming requests or apply rate-limit for unrecognized prefixes 3) purge and regen prefix cache after revert. trying 1 now.

cara: `/opsctl runtime set-config --pool us-west1 --continuous_batching false` -> applied.

sre-oncall: applied throttle on edge LB for suspect route (model-x /generate) to 50rps. CPU backpressure dropping. hopeful this buys time. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

devon: i can revert the normalization change immediately. will cut a rollback patch and push to canary. preparing PR: `revert(prompt_normalizer): use previous whitespace normalization`

leo: before full revert, can we also perform a safe fallback where prefix key generation tries old hash if new hash misses? that would avoid total regen. proposed pseudo: ```
function prefix_key(prompt) {
  k = new_hash(prompt);
  if (cache.has(k)) return k;
  k_old = old_hash(prompt);
  if (cache.has(k_old)) return k_old;
  return k;
}
```

eng-runtime: good call. but rollout path is longer. fastest is rollback + purge. I'll coordinate cache purge.

cara: running purge script now. `curl -X POST https://internal-cache.svc/purge_prefixes -d '{"pool":"us-west1","match":"promptkey:*"}'`

sre-oncall: purge returned 202 accepted. metrics show prefix cache size dropping 60% over 2 minutes. 5xx rate trending down to ~1.1x baseline. latency still elevated for long tails.

devon: rolling back normalization to previous behavior, push to canary now. PR merged, deploy in progress. commit `b2d4f00` is revert.

eng-runtime: once revert is live we should re-enable continuous batching but with reduced batch window to avoid a similar surge. config suggestion: `continuous_batch_window_ms: 15` and `max_batch_tokens: 512` -> temporarily `continuous_batch_window_ms: 5`, `max_batch_tokens: 256`.

cara: applying reduced batching config to us-west1 -> applied. monitoring.

sre-oncall: after rollback + purge + throttles, 5xx back to baseline, token throughput normalized. 95th latency improved ~220ms. leaving throttles in place for 30m.

cs-anna: heads up — we see increased retries from 4 customers (acct-233, acct-765, acct-998, acct-421). I will open support tickets and send the interim incident note. please tell me exact customer impact statement i can share.

cara: customer impact: transient increased 5xx and head-of-line latency for generation requests between 14:00-14:35 PDT for us-west1 routes. Some requests retried by clients causing higher cost. Approximately 4 customers saw >2x error rate; no data exfiltration.

cs-anna: sending note now and scheduling follow-ups. will add affected accounts to incident ticket.

eng-runtime: hotfix plan for next 24h: 1) keep old hash path as fallback (safe patch) 2) add unit tests around prompt_normalizer -> both whitespace and tokenization boundaries 3) add canary metrics for prefix key drift detection (alert when new_hash/new_key ratio > 0.02).

devon: will own the patch and tests. posting diff in #eng-runtime.

cara: creating incident record INC-2026 and postmortem doc at https://docs.company/INC-2026. please add timeline details and blame-free root cause analysis.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026 created by cara. Severity: P2. SLA impact flagged.

cara: handing off to eng-runtime (leo + devon) for remediation and follow-up. i'm available on pager if anything regresses. next on-call is `sre-oncall` in 30m; leaving throttles in place until then.

leo: acknowledged handoff. we'll track the roll-forward for the fallback hash and tests. will post updates in thread.

cara: thanks team — nice quick catch and coordinated mitigation. postmortem to include: why normalization change didn't trigger drift tests, why fallback path didn't exist, and why continuous batching amplified the issue.

sre-oncall: leaving a note: consider automatic cache-key-entropy guard in runtime so we detect sudden cardinality surges and auto-throttle before full meltdown.

eng-runtime: agreed, adding to roadmap.

cara: closing pager for now. monitoring window open for 2 hours. :white_check_mark:
